$comment: Maps Stream Deck actions onto Microsoft Teams meeting controls.
Teams' local third-party API (ws://localhost:8124) was retired on 2026-06-30
under MC1266901 with no replacement, so controls are driven through UI
Automation instead.
Entries here are MERGED OVER the plugin's built-in defaults, so you only need
to include the controls you want to change. Deleting this file is safe.
'automationId' values are locale-independent and are the preferred selector.
'activePattern' / 'inactivePattern' match the button's accessible NAME, which
IS localised - translate those to use state icons in another language. A
button's name describes the action it performs, so it is the inverse of the
current state: 'Unmute mic' means you are currently muted.
'menu' opens a flyout before looking for the item; 'submenu' opens one more
level inside it. '{arg}' in a menu item selector is replaced by the value the
key is configured with, which is how one translate control covers every
language.
'requiresRole' limits a control to a PowerPoint Live role, 'presenter' or
'attendee', so a key for the wrong role reports itself unavailable.
'stateFromSelection' reads state from UI Automation's selection rather than
from a label, which the drawing tools expose and which needs no translating.
'menuItemToggleAutomationId' is the id the same entry takes in its opposite
state, for menus Teams swaps rather than checks (Hide/Show presenter view).
NOTE: 'ppt-take-control' changes your ROLE. A successful press turns an
attendee into the presenter, so that key retires and every 'presenter' key
below becomes available. The sidecar re-reads state shortly after any press
so the keys follow the change.
NOTE: the zoom controls are shared but not symmetric - Teams labels them
'Magnify slide only for me' for an attendee and 'Magnify slide for all' for
the presenter. Zooming while presenting changes what everyone sees.
Captured from Teams 26255.500.5120.7530 on 2026-09-14, PowerPoint Live added
2026-09-17. After a Teams update, use the Diagnostics panel in any action's
property inspector to dump the live UI tree to the plugin log, then correct
the ids below and restart the plugin.
How a shared deck is recognised. The role is only exposed as a CSS class
on the slide-show root, so it is matched out of the class name - which
has the happy side effect of being locale-independent.
